events.description: A large, sudden explosion originates at the base of a concrete structure, producing a rapidly expanding fireball and dense plume of black smoke followed by a massive dust cloud that engulfs the building and spreads outward across the desert floor.

A large, sustained ground-level explosion in a desert environment, producing a rapidly expanding cloud of brown dust and darker smoke, with visible structural remnants (e.g., metal frame) at the epicenter in early frames. The blast evolves from an initial violent ejection of material to a massive, billowing plume that dominates the scene.

A large, sustained explosion generates a massive expanding plume of dark smoke and dust in an arid, hilly terrain; the blast origin is initially obscured but a structure becomes visible as the smoke clears slightly toward the end of the sequence.

A large, sustained explosion occurs at a fixed structure in a desert environment, producing a massive plume of dark smoke and dust that expands outward and upward over several seconds. The blast appears to originate from the base of the structure and progressively engulfs it.

A large, sustained dust and smoke plume erupts from the left side of a hardened structure in a desert test range, indicating a controlled explosion or blast impact. The plume expands and drifts rightward over time while the structure remains largely intact but obscured by debris and dust.

A large dust and smoke plume erupts and expands from the left side of a reinforced concrete structure, indicating a powerful ground-level explosion or blast event occurring near or within the building. The plume grows in volume and obscures part of the structure over time, with sustained dust ejection visible through all frames.
